text:
Priya: Quick follow-up from RFC review: we need an approach that lets customers without Privatelink support stay connected to our control plane without assigning per-tenant EIPs. Goal: minimal blast radius, preserve tenant src IP for audit, and keep rollout low-friction.

Liam: Can we enumerate concrete transport options and constraints? e.g., VXLAN/VxLAN over UDP, WireGuard, TLS over TCP proxy, or a regional relay with ephemeral mapping.

Nina: Constraints I keep hearing from Sales/Support:
- Some customers disallow kernel modules (no WireGuard).
- Some lock down UDP (only TCP 443 allowed).
- Others forbid adding transit IPs (no new EIPs).

Theo: That matches infra. Tradeoffs quick list:
- WireGuard/VXLAN: preserves src IP and L4 semantics, low overhead, but key mgmt + kernel deps.
- TLS-tcp proxy: very portable, uses cert infra, easier to run as a process, but typically requires SNAT or proxy-level mapping which breaks src IP.
- Regional relay: our infra terminates customer sessions centrally, can avoid per-tenant EIP by multiplexing but increases our egress/cost and requires sticky mapping logic.

Priya: Proposal: define a "shim negotiation" pattern. Installable shim attempts transports in order: 1) native encapsulation (vxlan/wg) -> preserves src, 2) UDP tunnel via DTLS -> if UDP allowed and no kernel, 3) TLS-tcp fallback -> worst case but always works. Shim records which transport is active and advertises that to the control plane for routing decisions.

Liam: How do we preserve src IP with TLS-tcp fallback? Could the local shim inject tenant identity into a header the agent trusts (not source IP), and we map that for logging? Not ideal for audit, but pragmatic.

Nina: Agree. Add a signed metadata envelope on agent registration so downstream systems can attribute traffic even if src IP is lost. Must capture at least tenant id, agent id, install timestamp, and shim transport.

ops-bot: note: link to previous cost spike: https://ci/internal/relays/egress-cost-model.csv (uploaded)

Theo: Security and compliance: mutual TLS for TLS-tcp, and short-lived keys for UDP/WG. Need attestation: shim presents signed install manifest on startup. Add SSM/KMS integration options for key storage.

Priya: Observability: shim MUST expose: local metrics (prometheus), a /debug/state (authz token), and emit structured registration events when transport changes. We should add tracing headers and span IDs.

Liam: Rollout rules: default in Private offering = disabled. Offer as opt-in beta for customers with specific network restrictions. Pilot customers must pass an e2e connectivity matrix (privatelink down; shim up; verify agent->cp traffic; verify logs/attribution).

Nina: Failure modes: if shim loses connectivity we must avoid blackholing: agent should fall back to existing path (privatelink) and circuit-break to prevent flapping. Recommend counters: consecutive failures threshold = 5, cooldown = 10m.

Priya: Implementation spikes and owners:
- spike/wg-preserve-src (Liam + Theo) 1d to check kernel vs userspace options and perf.
- spike/dtls-udp (Nina) d to validate UDP fallback without kernel modules.
- spike/tls-proxy-envelope (Priya) d to define signed metadata envelope and obs contract.

Theo: Add tests: src-IP fidelity tests, signed-envelope verification, transport negotiation instrumentation, and end-to-end latency p50/p95 comparison against privatelink.

ops-bot: created ticket RELAY-SHIM-101 with checklist and security review slot: https://tickets/internal/RELAY-SHIM-101

Liam: Cost note: regional relays help customers that ban egress, but we need a chargeback model (meter relay hours + egress). Finance wants a simple per-GB uplift for relay usage.

Nina: Also note cloud provider specifics: AWS Privatelink + TGW interplay will require special routing for VXLAN; Azure Private Endpoint blocks certain UDP paths; GCP PSC often needs internal DNS mapping. We should document provider caveats in the README for each shim mode.

Priya: One more: Dedicated customers -> shim must be able to point to dedicated CP endpoints. Add a config flag install-time: "control_plane_endpoint" which can be hosted or dedicated.

Theo: I'll draft the shim negotiation state machine and a minimal config schema.

Priya: Action items:
- @Liam/@Theo: start wg spike (1w) and post perf notes.
- @Nina: DTLS/UDP feasibility (1w) + provider caveats doc.
- @Priya: design signed envelope and obs contract (3d).
- schedule pilot kick-off after spikes.

Liam: thumbs up. I'll create the repo skeleton and a minimal Docker image for the userspace shim this afternoon.

Priya: Thanks all. We'll reconvene next Monday to pick the default mode for beta.
